topic: The reciprocity rule: why favors and free samples work
title: The Reciprocity Rule: Why Favors Create Debts
voiceover: Does getting a small favor make us want to give something back? In 1971, Dennis Regan ran an experiment in which people rated paintings. During a break, a partner of the researcher, Joe, sometimes returned with a Coke for the participant. Later, Joe asked participants to buy raffle tickets. Participants who got the favor bought more tickets than those who did not. This held even when they said they didn't like Joe. Regan linked the result to a norm of reciprocity: we feel we should repay. It was one laboratory experiment. Applying it to free samples in stores is an extension, not something this study tested. So a small favor may create a pull to repay, even toward someone you don't like. Tomorrow: why do we judge other people's character but explain away our own behavior?
